title: Infosys Ltd - 500209 - Announcement Under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Infosys cut FY27 cc revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3% from 1.5%–3.5% after Q1 cc growth of 2.4% YoY; margin guidance held at 20%–22%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was $5,082 mn, up 1% QoQ and 2.4% YoY in constant currency, with a one-off 50 bps hit from a EURS client program termination. Operating margin rose 20 bps QoQ to 21.1%, helped by 70 bps rupee tailwind and 20 bps from Project Maximus, while large deal TCV was $3.6 bn with 61% net new. Management cut the revenue range on softer volumes, weaker pricing from AI-led productivity asks and competition, and offshoring/onsite-mix shifts. The Board also named Ashiss Dash as CEO-designate, succeeding Salil Parekh on April 1, 2027.

61% net new; 22 large deals, 3 worth ~$400 mn each
up from 5.5% in Q3 FY26 per management

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: Management expects FS growth above company average for the rest of FY27; ~$1 bn of large deal net new TCV and 5 large deal wins in FS and Communications combined.

segments.name: EURS
segments.commentary: Q1 hit by a one-off program termination (~50 bps); adjusted growth described as strong, and EURS expected to grow above company average.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew ~1.5% reported (1% cc per editor's note) despite a large European auto client decline; 3 large deal wins.

segments.name: Retail and CPG
segments.commentary: Consumer spend muted; large deal pipeline healthy but decision cycles longer; one of two segments flagged as still challenged along with Communications.

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Operating environment challenging; clients prioritising near-term AI gains; one of two segments flagged as challenged.

segments.name: Life Sciences / Healthcare
segments.commentary: Expected benefit from the Optimum Healthcare acquisition (~1.7% contribution to FY27 revenue guidance from Optimum Healthcare and Stratus).

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth cut to 1.5%–3% YoY from prior 1.5%–3.5%; guidance includes ~1.7% from acquisitions (Optimum Healthcare, Stratus), slightly over 1% drag from a European manufacturing client, and 0.75%–1% from offshore shift.
Like-to-like organic guidance midpoint implied at ~0.8% versus ~2.2% at the prior midpoint, per the BNP Paribas exchange; management did not dispute the arithmetic.
Operating margin guidance maintained at 20%–22%, assuming wage-hike headwinds, AI investments and ~50 bps acquisition impact, offset by Project Maximus and currency.
Onsite mix excluding acquisitions expected to fall 75 bps to 1% for the year, a margin tailwind.
Salary hikes effective October for most employees, with the rest in January 2027.
Lower end of revenue guidance assumes further macro deterioration; top end assumes improvement, but less than assumed in April.
capex_capacity: Plan to hire 20,000 college graduates in FY27, matching FY26; over 4,000 hired in Q1 FY27.
Target of 6,000 Frontier Engineers over the next few years, mainly built through college hiring and internal reskilling.
Management decided not to enter AI infrastructure or data center business at this stage after internal board review.
No staff restructuring; reskilling done across the workforce, per management.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective; priorities are AI, modernization, cloud, productivity and consolidation, with discretionary spend scrutinised.
Pricing softer than expected: client productivity asks tied to AI plus rising competition; management says net pricing still increased.
AI-led deflation is a headwind at renewals and on non-large deals; management tracks compression internally but does not quantify it externally.
Six consolidation deals won, representing ~$700 mn net new; 20% of large deal TCV from vendor consolidation.
Management cites a conscious decision to walk away from European manufacturing deals that did not meet return thresholds.
Outcome-based pricing discussions increasing but not a large share of activity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the upper end of revenue guidance lower and what is the macro view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 volumes were soft through the quarter, one-off EURS termination came late in the quarter, and a European client deal was declined on economics; the upper end now assumes a less favourable macro recovery than in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-time program termination fully absorbed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said what is known has been taken in Q1, with no further known Q2 impact from that program.

qa_highlights.question: Can the AI deflation be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not quantify compression externally; it says contract scope is often redefined and adjacent work offsets some of it.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given wage hikes and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 wage-hike impact is lower than FY26 since FY26 carried a full-year effect of the April hike; currency, Project Maximus and lower onsite mix offset it, and 20%–22% guidance is held.

qa_highlights.question: Will headcount grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said headcount will grow with revenue over time; no year-end headcount guidance was given and recruitment continues.

qa_highlights.question: Rupee impact on margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Every 1% rupee depreciation gives 15–17 bps margin benefit; ~45% revenue comes from non-US geographies, which partly offsets this.

risks_watch: Guidance is conditional on macro; the lower end assumes further deterioration, and pricing pressure from AI productivity asks could persist.
Q2 carry-over from soft Q1 volumes and the European manufacturing client's Q4 deal closure in December.
Undisclosed AI deflation on existing book; watch renewals and whether AI-first revenue growth (8.2%) keeps pace.
CEO transition: Salil Parekh's term ends March 31, 2027; Ashiss Dash takes over April 1, 2027 after a 6-month mentorship from October 1.
Attrition rising to 13% and talent competition from hyperscalers and AI services start-ups for Frontier Engineers.
Margin headwinds from acquisition amortisation, founder retention payouts and H2 wage hikes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI strategy, margins and large deals, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the revenue cut, attributing it to macro uncertainty, client-specific events and pricing. Management avoided quantifying AI deflation and declined to comment on specific renewal losses.
key_quotes: Our AI services revenue was 8.2% of overall revenue in Q1.
So all of those are tailwinds, puts-and-takes all of that put together, we are still very confident of maintaining our margin guidance.
On the AI, I think there is a huge differentiation that I find from what we are working on.
we will compete aggressively in the market, but we are not going to underwrite uneconomic productivity assumptions.

growth.why: FY27 cc revenue guidance cut to 1.5%–3% (midpoint 2.25%) from 1.5%–3.5%, with Q1 cc growth of 2.4% YoY; backing is partial, citing a $3.6 bn large deal TCV (61% net new), acquisitions (~1.7%) and 6,000 Frontier Engineer hiring, but no specific capacity additions, and management disavowed AI infrastructure investment.

mgmt.note: Board named Ashiss Dash as CEO-designate, succeeding Salil Parekh on April 1, 2027; no stated growth plan from him on this call.
